section_summary: This section follows investigations of Aikoku Doshi Kai, a Japanese nationalist society in Peru whose members rejected Japan’s defeat in the Second World War. Reports describe its links to Shindo Remmei in Brazil, meetings led by Kenzo Abe, threats against dissenters, and arrests in August 1946. Later documents cover Peruvian expulsion orders, requests for U.S. help with deportation, Abe’s public appeals, and a longer investigative report that continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: New Japanese Secret Society Formed in Lima to Perpetuate Ideals of Japanese War Mongers
subfiles.about: Reports the formation of Aikoku Doshi Kai and forwards a Legal Attaché report.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes meetings, fundraising, defeat denial and concern among Japanese residents about possible intimidation.

subfiles.title: Aikoku Doshi Kai, also known as Aikoku Dishi Kay
subfiles.about: Investigates the society’s founders, activities and links to Japanese organizers from Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Sources identify founders and officers, describe an unsuccessful application to form a mutual aid society, and report secret meetings addressed by a man called Abe or Matsushima. They describe his claims that Japan won the war, alleged threats against dissenters and links to Shindo Remmei in Brazil.

subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip
subfiles.about: Routes the preceding material within the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Internal routing slip.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Aikoku Doshi Kai
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential memorandum on the Japanese society in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends an informant’s memorandum and notes that U.S. embassies in Rio de Janeiro and Lima received the information.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Aikoku Doshi Kai, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Duplicates Hoover’s transmittal of the confidential society memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the preceding letter.

subfiles.title: Confidential memorandum on Aikoku Doshi Kai
subfiles.about: Details the society’s founders, meetings, financing and Brazilian connections.
subfiles.summary: This copy substantially repeats the July 11 Legal Attaché report. It describes a purported mutual aid front, money collected in Lima, meetings led by Abe or Matsushima, claims that Japan won the war, and concern that dissenting Japanese residents might face reprisals.

subfiles.title: Arrests of Kenzo Abe and Japanese society members
subfiles.about: Reports arrests and seized materials following a meeting in Huaral.
subfiles.summary: Peruvian police arrested Abe, Torigoe and about 25 others; the embassy reports seized films, documents, alleged threats and a possible request for U.S. deportation assistance.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the arrests of Kenzo Abe and Takeshi Torigoe
subfiles.about: Forwards a paraphrase of the Lima telegram to the War Department.
subfiles.summary: Neal highlights Peru’s possible request for U.S. help repatriating Abe and Torigoe.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Lima Telegram No. 884
subfiles.about: Summarizes the arrests and investigation of Aikoku Doshi Kai.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of the August 16 telegram about arrests, seized material, intimidation and possible deportation.

subfiles.title: Arrest of Organizers and Members of Japanese Nationalistic Society in Peru
subfiles.about: Transmits the Legal Attaché’s detailed post-arrest investigation.
subfiles.summary: The despatch outlines the society’s constitution, arrests, documents seized from Abe, his interrogation and the likelihood of a Peruvian deportation request.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Ambassador: Aikoku Doshi Kai
subfiles.about: Presents supplementary evidence gathered after the arrests of Abe and Torigoe.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum identifies officers, founders, detainees, alleged opponents and contributors to a proposed women’s organization, and reproduces the society’s constitution. It traces Abe and Torigoe’s journey from Brazil to Peru and summarizes their sometimes inconsistent accounts of Shindo Remmei and their mission. It also records seized films and publications and discusses possible deportation.

subfiles.title: Expulsion of Abe Kenso and Takeshi Torigoe
subfiles.about: Reports Peru’s authorization to expel Abe and Torigoe.
subfiles.summary: The despatch forwards a Supreme Resolution citing illegal entry and activities contrary to public order.

subfiles.title: Expulsión de japoneses
subfiles.about: Authorizes the expulsion of Abe Kenso or Matzushima and Takeshi Torigoe.
subfiles.summary: Resolution published in El Peruano on September 3.

subfiles.title: Expulsion of Kintaro Kobayashi
subfiles.about: Reports Peru’s order to expel Aikoku Doshi Kai secretary Kintaro Kobayashi.
subfiles.summary: The embassy describes Kobayashi as a founder, detainee and dangerous local society member.

subfiles.title: Expulsión de extranjeros por indeseables
subfiles.about: Authorizes Kintaro Kobayashi’s expulsion as an undesirable foreign national.
subfiles.summary: Resolution published in El Peruano on September 25.

subfiles.title: Peruvian request for help deporting three Japanese nationals
subfiles.about: Relays Peru’s request for U.S. assistance deporting Abe, Torigoe and Kobayashi.
subfiles.summary: Cooper suggests the War Department might provide transport and custody facilities.

subfiles.title: Questions concerning transport of three deportees
subfiles.about: Requests practical details needed to arrange transportation.
subfiles.summary: State asks who will pay transport and custody costs and when the three men will be ready.

subfiles.title: Acknowledging receipt of Japanese newspapers
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consulate General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Acknowledges newspapers sent with three Department instructions.
subfiles.summary: Cross confirms receipt of the Japanese newspapers.

subfiles.title: Acknowledging receipt of Japanese newspapers, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Duplicates the consular acknowledgment of Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the preceding acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Abe Kenso appeals to the President of Peru
subfiles.about: Reports Abe’s public appeal against detention and deportation.
subfiles.summary: Abe claims to be a Japanese envoy, requests an audience and provisional liberty, and denies terrorist activity. The embassy forwards press clippings.

subfiles.title: Press fragment concerning Abe Kenso
subfiles.about: Mentions Abe’s request to explain his journey to Peruvian officials.
subfiles.summary: Brief Spanish press fragment about Abe’s requested audience.

subfiles.title: El Comercio report on Abe Kenso’s petition
subfiles.about: Reports Abe’s request to meet Peru’s president or foreign minister.
subfiles.summary: The article discusses his petition, provisional liberty and official investigation.

subfiles.title: Carta de Abe Kenso
subfiles.about: Abe explains his claimed mission in Peru and contests his detention.
subfiles.summary: Abe says he came to counsel Japanese residents accused of dishonoring the flag and emperor, denies terrorism and asks for an official audience.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal of confidential communication
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential report for Neal’s information.
subfiles.summary: Hoover attaches information from a confidential source.

subfiles.title: Confidential report on Aikoku Doshi Kai and related Japanese societies
subfiles.about: Compiles evidence on the Lima society, Abe’s activities and a related society in Huancayo.
subfiles.summary: The report expands on Aikoku Doshi Kai’s officers, constitution, propaganda, membership, arrests and seized records. It recounts Abe’s route through Bolivia, his interrogations, alleged fundraising for a delegation to Japan, and a proposed women’s auxiliary. It also reproduces the constitution and part of the founder list for a similar Japanese society in Huancayo. The report continues beyond page 113.
